analyst.summary: Hitachi Energy India has nearly doubled over six months (ret_6m ~98%) on a genuinely strong FY26 print -- revenue +27.6% YoY to Rs 8,147.7cr, PAT +157.3% to Rs 987.8cr, record order backlog of Rs 29,555.3cr (+53.5% YoY) -- but the backlog surge traces overwhelmingly to a single Q1 FY26 mega-order (the Bhadla-Fatehpur HVDC link plus a POWERGRID bulk transformer order, which alone drove +365% YoY order growth that quarter); every subsequent FY26 quarter reverted to an ordinary run-rate (+13.6%, an adjusted +73.7% off a soft headline, +10.6%), full-year order inflow grew just 1.6% YoY, and the backlog itself was flat for four straight quarters. The PAT surge is likewise dominated by margin normalization off a depressed FY25 base (EBITDA margin 4% to 13% through FY25, now 15-17%) rather than pure volume growth, and reported FCF yield is just 0.17% -- cash conversion lagging the P&L on heavy capex (Rs 4,000cr transformer capacity, funded in part by a Rs 2,520.82cr March-2025 QIP that diluted the promoter from 75% to 71.31%) and working-capital absorption typical of long-gestation HVDC projects. At roughly 144-151x trailing earnings and ~28x book, the stock is the richest name in its own three-way HVDC oligopoly (GE Vernova T&D ~96-101x TTM, ABB India's own core multiple ~86-99x), and even the most bullish sell-side targets (JM Financial Rs 38,000, Kotak Rs 36,000, both Neutral) imply only modest upside from an already-rich multiple. The India transmission-capex supercycle (Rs 9.15 lakh crore to 2032, $14-15bn of HVDC orders over five to six years per JPMorgan) is real and the franchise quality (zero debt, AAA rated, 29% ROCE) is not in question -- this is a valuation call on an existing holding, not a franchise-quality call, and it is flagged as a genuine Hold-vs-Sell tension against the quant model's own Hold.
